title: Tail Quantiles: attribution pipeline, regression detectors, and per-route/model/region dashboards
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Goal: Build a production-ready attribution pipeline and dashboard surfaces that expose p95 and p99 latency slices per API route, model variant, and region, with automated regression detection tied into the existing load-test harness. This ticket covers: 1) ingestion and storage model for tail quantiles, 2) dashboard UX for filtering and drilldowns, 3) alerting rules and regression detection thresholds, and 4) integration with tokens/sec and synthetic load test profiles.

Motivation: Engineers frequently need to find why tail latency increases for a given endpoint (route) and model combination in a particular region. Current dashboards show coarse rollups and token-level metrics separately; we need a unified view to attribute p95/p99 regressions to route/model/region and trigger timely investigation.

Scope: - Instrument request path to emit per-request latency histogram summary (HdrHistogram sketches) and token counts. - Create an ingestion job that reduces HdrHistogram sketches into time-windowed rollups (1m, 5m, 1h) keyed by route:model:region. - Store rollups in metrics backend (Influx/ClickHouse) with efficient retention and pre-aggregated quantiles. - Implement frontend visualizations in Console: heatmap overview, timeline per-slice, linked traces/trace-id list, and quick links to load-test profiles. - Implement a regression detector that compares current p95/p99 to a dynamic baseline and creates alerts/annotations in the dashboard when regressions exceed configurable thresholds.

Out of scope: Long-term cardinality work for user-level attribution; raw request payload storage for privacy reasons (we will only keep metadata and sketches).
acceptance_criteria: p95 and p99 values available in Console for any combination of route, model, and region with 1m/5m/1h rollups
Heatmap overview shows top 50 route:model:region slices by p99 and tokens/sec over the selected window
Regression detector raises an alert and dashboard annotation when p95 or p99 increases by >20% vs 7-day baseline for a slice
Load-test job (k8s) can push synthetic traffic and the system correctly attributes observed tail latency to the expected slice
Instrumentation emits tokens/request and per-request HdrHistogram summary; storage cost within forecast by <10%

notes: Design decisions: prefer HdrHistogram sketching at the edge to avoid high cardinality histograms in Prometheus; we will roll up sketches into ClickHouse for quantile extraction. Prometheus will continue to hold coarse counters (tokens/sec).

Trade-offs considered: t-digest vs HdrHistogram: HdrHistogram chosen for its high-resolution tail accuracy and low CPU cost for merges. t-digest has smaller footprints for median but worse tail fidelity.

Storage estimate: anticipated additional storage ~2TB/month for 90-day retention across all rollups (pre-aggregation windowing applied). We will evaluate retention/aggregation if cost exceeds projections.
Privacy: sketches contain only latency buckets and no user payloads. We will add a flag to disable sketching for privacy-sensitive customers (Private deployments).

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Tail+Quantile+Attribution (draft), GitHub PR for SDK summarizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287
